description:
Construction of a single-storey brick extension at the rear of the building that extends 4.45m, 3,00m high overall.
The property is an end-of-terrace 1960s residential home with an already existing rear extension. It is located on a linear site facing Glebe
Way and is set back from the main road by a front garden and driveway. The property is surrounded by mature trees and greenery and is part
of a street of similar terrace homes, many of which also have rear extensions.
The proposed scheme involves creating a new family Kitchen, Living and Dining area by extending the rear of the property. This frees up
space at the front to create a new guest bedroom, with the downstairs bathroom. The proposed facade
will feature new brick that matches the existing stock, and the frames will be painted to match the retained windows. New sliding doors will
provide access to the garden, and a new bedroom window will be created for the front facade. 
The single storey brick lean-to at the rear of the building will be retained and will remain separate without adjoining to the proposed rear extension.
The side entrance will be retained in the same facade but relocated to provide access to the living room and new kitchen.
decision_conditions:
This proposal CONSTITUTES DEVELOPMENT within the meaning of Section 55 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, but by virtue of Article 3 and Schedule 2 of the Town and Country (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 and any subsequent legislative amendments is of a class which is described as PERMITTED DEVELOPMENT and therefore planning permission IS NOT REQUIRED subject to the following conditions:

(a)	the materials used in any exterior work (other than materials used in the construction of a conservatory) shall be of a similar appearance to those used in the construction of the exterior of the existing dwellinghouse;
(b)	any upper-floor window located in a wall or roof slope forming a side elevation of the dwellinghouse shall be:
	(i)	obscure-glazed, and
	(ii)	non-opening unless the parts of the window which can be opened are more than 1.7 metres above the floor of the room in which the window is installed; and
(c)	where the enlarged part of the dwellinghouse has more than one storey, the roof pitch of the enlarged part shall, so far as practicable, be the same as the roof pitch of the original dwellinghouse.
